title: Idempotent
body:
An operation is idempotent if performing it many times has the same effect as performing it once. This matters for [[HTTP]] because networks are unreliable: if a response is lost, a client (or a proxy, or a retry layer) may send the same request again, and idempotency is what makes that safe.

GET, PUT, DELETE, and HEAD are idempotent — fetching a resource five times, or setting it to the same value five times, or deleting it five times, leaves the same end state. POST is **not** idempotent: five identical POSTs typically create five records, which is exactly why double-clicking a submit button can produce duplicate orders. PATCH is not guaranteed idempotent, because a partial update like "increment the counter" changes the state each time.

Note that idempotent is not the same as *safe*: GET is both safe (no side effects at all) and idempotent, while DELETE is idempotent but definitely not safe. See [[HTTP Verb]].
